# AgentPay

> AgentPay is an authorization and enforcement layer for agent purchases. It lets a user create a narrow payment mandate, approve it with a passkey, and revoke it immediately.

## Public entry points

- [Landing page](https://agentpay-yuno.vercel.app/): what AgentPay does, for buyers and for merchants.
- [Privacy Policy](https://agentpay-yuno.vercel.app/privacy): how AgentPay handles personal information.
- [Terms of Service](https://agentpay-yuno.vercel.app/terms): the terms governing use of AgentPay.
- [Connect an MCP client](https://agentpay-yuno.vercel.app/connect): user-facing instructions for connecting an authenticated agent.
- [Merchant demo](https://agentpay-yuno.vercel.app/store): an example merchant checkout experience.
- [MCP endpoint](https://agentpay-yuno.vercel.app/mcp): OAuth-protected Streamable HTTP MCP server.
- [MCP protected-resource metadata](https://agentpay-yuno.vercel.app/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource): OAuth discovery for the MCP endpoint.
- [Merchant discovery example](https://agentpay-yuno.vercel.app/.well-known/agentpay.json): an example of a merchant-owned AgentPay manifest.
- [Merchant documentation](https://agentpay-yuno.vercel.app/docs): how a store installs and sets up the AgentPay merchant SDK.
- [Merchant console](https://agentpay-yuno.vercel.app/developers): register a merchant ID, create a hosted test store, manage products and keys, and inspect checkout decisions.
- [Supported live stores](https://agentpay-yuno.vercel.app/api/stores): verified public store and discovery URLs. This list is empty until a real merchant verifies and opts in.

## Identity and fraud boundary

- Account holders complete a hosted Didit v3 identity and fraud-verification workflow before authorizing a mandate or one-time exception.
- AgentPay stores only Didit's minimal session and entity status. Documents, images, biometrics, provider tokens, and the full decision are not copied into AgentPay.
- Didit webhooks are timestamp-bounded, HMAC-verified, de-duplicated, and reconciled against the decision API after the hosted redirect.

- [Framework recipes](https://agentpay-yuno.vercel.app/docs/frameworks): Next.js, Hono, Express, Fastify and edge runtimes.

- [SDK reference](https://agentpay-yuno.vercel.app/docs/reference): exported functions and types.

- [Decisions and reason codes](https://agentpay-yuno.vercel.app/docs/reference/decisions): every outcome a merchant can receive.
- [Troubleshooting](https://agentpay-yuno.vercel.app/docs/troubleshooting): the failures merchants actually hit.
- [Merchant console and stores](https://agentpay-yuno.vercel.app/docs/stores): merchant onboarding, hosted test URLs, API keys, and supported live-store policy.

## Agent operating rules

- Authenticate to the MCP endpoint before using tools.
- Discover products on store-owned pages. AgentPay's supported-store endpoint contains only verified URLs; it is not a copied catalog or product-ranking directory.
- Start with `get_account`. If identity verification is required, direct the user to its `verification_url` and wait for the hosted Didit flow. If payment setup is required, use the browser link returned by `get_payment_setup_link` and never request card numbers, CVCs, PINs, bank passwords, or vault credentials in chat.
- Create the narrowest mandate that matches the user's request, then wait for the user to approve it with a passkey before purchasing.
- Express every product price and mandate limit in USD integer cents. AgentPay does not convert currencies.
- A purchase outside an active mandate must be escalated for a one-time approval. Do not retry a refused purchase without that approval.
- Revoke the mandate immediately when the user asks to stop.

## Indexing boundary

The sitemap intentionally contains only public HTML pages. APIs, OAuth flows, the MCP transport, authenticated screens, payment setup and registry endpoints are protocol surfaces rather than crawlable content; their supported methods and trust boundaries are listed in the route inventory.
